title: Standard Practices — Release of the Chromate-Free Surface Protection Process to In-Service Work
abstract: Release of the chromate-free conversion coating and primer process to repair stations, with the qualification coupon regime and the approval extension needed before it may be used on in-service structural work.

sections.planning_reason: Authorisation for the continued industrial use of hexavalent chromium is being withdrawn progressively and several detail-part suppliers have already stopped offering the chromated process. Repair stations that re-protect a joint after structural work therefore need a compliant alternative, and modifications released after the process change assume it. Without this bulletin a station has no approved way of restoring the protection on a joint it has opened.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin releases the chromate-free surface protection process for in-service work. It specifies the trivalent chromium conversion coating, the chromate-free epoxy primer, the cure schedule and the adhesion coupon regime, and it defines the approval extension a station must hold before applying the process to a structural joint.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Confirm that the station holds the extended approval for the chromate-free process. Set up the process line to the parameters of drawing D51201131570 and record the bath chemistry. Prepare an adhesion coupon on the reference article D5120112339055 at the start of each shift and process it with the work. Clean and deoxidise the joint surfaces. Apply the trivalent chromium conversion coating for the immersion time given, then rinse and dry within the stated window. Apply the chromate-free epoxy primer to the specified film thickness and cure to the schedule. Test the shift coupon for adhesion after the humidity soak and record the result. Where the coupon fails, quarantine all work processed in that shift. Replace any grommet AES445369-54 disturbed during the work, because its silicone compound is not compatible with the new primer cure. Record the process against the joint in the aircraft technical record.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all ZEPHYR-22 family aircraft and to any joint opened during repair or modification. There is no aircraft effectivity in the usual sense: the bulletin releases a process rather than modifying an aircraft, and it is embodied per joint rather than per aircraft.
sections.material_note: No kit. The conversion coating and primer are ordered as process chemicals with a six-month shelf life. Reference articles for the coupon regime are supplied one per station and are re-usable. The bracket D5120116861898 is supplied as the coupon carrier for stations that cannot mount the reference article directly.

type_data.compliance_time: Before any structural joint is re-protected using the chromate-free process; otherwise no compliance date applies.

title: Standard Practices — Release of the Chromate-Free Surface Protection Process to In-Service Work

issue.reason: The bulletin is re-issued as a recommended bulletin and the shift coupon regime is written as an instruction rather than as guidance.

abstract: Release of the chromate-free conversion coating and primer process to repair stations, re-issued as a recommended bulletin so that the adhesion coupon regime the structural substantiation rests on is an instruction and not advice.

sections.planning_reason: Authorisation for the continued industrial use of hexavalent chromium is being withdrawn progressively and several detail-part suppliers have already stopped offering the chromated process. Repair stations that re-protect a joint after structural work therefore need a compliant alternative, and modifications released after the process change assume it. Without this bulletin a station has no approved way of restoring the protection on a joint it has opened.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin releases the chromate-free surface protection process for in-service work. It specifies the trivalent chromium conversion coating, the chromate-free epoxy primer, the cure schedule and the adhesion coupon regime, and it defines the approval extension a station must hold before applying the process to a structural joint.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Confirm that the station holds the extended approval for the chromate-free process. Set up the process line to the parameters of drawing D51201131570 and record the bath chemistry. Prepare an adhesion coupon on the reference article D5120112339055 at the start of each shift and process it with the work; this is a required step and not a recommended practice, because the adhesion data behind every structural substantiation that uses this process assumes one coupon per shift. Clean and deoxidise the joint surfaces. Apply the trivalent chromium conversion coating for the immersion time given, then rinse and dry within the stated window. Apply the chromate-free epoxy primer to the specified film thickness and cure to the schedule. Test the shift coupon for adhesion after the humidity soak and record the result against the shift. Where the coupon fails, quarantine all work processed in that shift and do not release it; a shift without a tested coupon is treated as a failed shift. Replace any grommet AES445369-54 disturbed during the work, because its silicone compound is not compatible with the new primer cure. Record the process and the coupon result against the joint in the aircraft technical record.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all ZEPHYR-22 family aircraft and to any joint opened during repair or modification. There is no aircraft effectivity in the usual sense: the bulletin releases a process rather than modifying an aircraft, and it is embodied per joint rather than per aircraft. What has changed at this issue is its status: the first issue released the process for information, which left a station free to apply it without running the coupon regime, and the substantiation does not stand on that basis.
sections.material_note: No kit. The conversion coating and primer are ordered as process chemicals with a six-month shelf life. Reference articles for the coupon regime are supplied one per station and are re-usable, and a station must hold at least one before it starts work, because the regime is now a condition of the release. The bracket D5120116861898 is supplied as the coupon carrier for stations that cannot mount the reference article directly.

type_data.compliance_time: Before any structural joint is re-protected using the chromate-free process. A station applying the process must hold the extended approval and must run the coupon regime from the first shift.

revision_history.reason: Re-issued as a recommended bulletin with the adhesion coupon regime written as an instruction and the quarantine rule made explicit
